confirmed.quote: A 1.21 server reports its own sprinting speed modifier; prismarine-physics keeps it next to its own
confirmed.correction: A 1.21 server sends its own sprint modifier, and prismarine-physics 1.11.1 would keep it next to its own, because it strips only the old sprint UUID. With Mineflayer 4.39 and minecraft-data 3.117, though, the attribute is stored under an outdated 'generic.*' key (movement_speed, id 21, arrives as 'generic.step_height'). Prismarine-physics never reads it and already sprints at 1.3 times walking speed. The bot's removal of the server's movement-speed attribute never fires (its log line appears in none of the live logs).

confirmed.quote: an unmodified bot sprints at 1.3 x 1.3 instead of 1.3 times walking speed
confirmed.correction: With these library versions an unmodified bot already sprints at 1.3 times walking speed. Mineflayer stores the server's movement-speed attribute under a protocol name ("generic.*") that prismarine-physics never reads (it looks for "minecraft:movement_speed"), so prismarine always uses its default speed plus its own sprint modifier. The double modifier (1.3 x 1.3) would happen only if those keys matched. The bot's step that removes the server-sent attribute is a safeguard that never ran in any live run.

confirmed.quote: The bot removes the server-sent movement-speed attribute before each tick
confirmed.correction: After every physics tick the bot runs a check that would delete a server-sent movement-speed attribute. In the recorded live runs it never found one: minecraft-data 3.117.0's 1.21.4 protocol mapper stores the server's movement_speed (id 21) under the key 'generic.step_height'. Neither this check nor prismarine-physics (which reads 'minecraft:movement_speed') sees it, so prismarine uses its default speed with its own sprint modifier. That matches the vanilla client and the simulator.

confirmed.quote: The environment step makes no host synchronisation
confirmed.correction: The environment step never reads values back from the GPU: it has no .item(), .cpu() or .tolist() calls and no Python branches on tensor values. One small blocking host-to-device copy remains, torch.tensor(WINDOW, device=dev) in physics._Cells, which runs twice per tick. Precomputing it once as a device constant would remove the step's last synchronisation. With 16,384 parallel courses, one RTX 5080 simulates about one million game ticks per second.

sprinting speed modifier, which prismarine-physics keeps next to its own
confirmed.correction: A 1.21 server sends the player's movement_speed attribute with its own 'minecraft:sprinting' modifier. Its id differs from prismarine-physics' UUID, so the two would stack (1.3 x 1.3) if prismarine-physics read that attribute. With the installed minecraft-data 3.117.0 it never does: the attribute decodes under the key 'generic.step_height' (an old id table), not 'minecraft:movement_speed'. So an unmodified bot already sprints at 1.3 times walking speed, as the vanilla client and the simulator do. The bot's removal of 'movement_speed' keys is only a safeguard and has no effect with this stack.

confirmed.quote: an unmodified bot sprints 1.3 x 1.3 times as fast as walking instead of 1.3
confirmed.correction: If prismarine-physics read the server's movement-speed attribute, the server's sprinting modifier would stack with prismarine's own and give 1.3 x 1.3 = 1.69 times walking speed. With the pinned versions (mineflayer 4.39.0, minecraft-data 3.117.0, prismarine-physics 1.11.1) it never reads it: the attribute arrives under a 'generic.*' key (in fact 'generic.step_height'), not 'minecraft:movement_speed'. So even an unmodified bot sprints at 1.3 times walking, the same as the vanilla client and the simulator. The bridge's removal step never fires.

confirmed.quote: The bot removes the server-sent movement-speed attribute before every tick
confirmed.correction: After each physics tick (so before the next one), the bot deletes any attribute whose key contains 'movement_speed'. With the installed minecraft-data (3.117.0), the 1.21.4 attribute IDs are stale: the server's movement-speed attribute (id 21) is stored under 'generic.step_height', so nothing is actually removed, and the removal log line never appears in any live run. It makes no difference: prismarine-physics looks for 'minecraft:movement_speed', never finds the server's attribute, and uses its default walk speed plus its own sprint modifier. That matches the vanilla client and the simulator (live replays match to 2e-14 blocks).

disputed_items.quote: the fall penalty speeds up learning
disputed_items.correction: Reward terms interact with risk: the fall penalty does not speed up early learning (both arms reach 80% test success at 0.05 B ticks, and without it the agent is level or slightly ahead for the first ~250 iterations). Instead it keeps the policy improving after the no-fall arm levels off near 91%, which raises the final score (93.3 vs 90.9%) and the hardest-level score (72.0 vs 55.2%), and the curriculum reaches level 5 sooner. On very tight jumps (single neos), though, it teaches the agent to refuse.
